problems.title: The other quadratic root
problems.question: x²+x+a=0 has root −1. Find the other root.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Root sum is −1.
steps: Thus the other root is −1−(−1)=0. Substitution also gives a=0, confirming roots −1,0.

problems.title: Separation of two roots
problems.question: Find the absolute difference of roots of 2x²−3x−2=0.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Factor(2x+1)(x−2)=0.
steps: The roots are −1/2,2, separated by 2.5.

problems.title: Two negative roots in ratio3
problems.question: x²+bx+12=0 has negative roots in ratio3. Find b.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Write roots t,3t, t<0. Their product 3t²=12 gives t=−2.
steps: The roots are −2,−6, whose sum −8 equals −b. Thus b=8.

problems.title: Check an impossible trigonometric condition
problems.question: Evaluate(tanα+cotα)/(0.6tanαcotα) if sinαcosα=2/3.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: For real α,|sinαcosα|=|sin2α|/2≤1/2.
steps: The stated value2/3 is impossible, so there is no real angle satisfying the conditions.
Formal substitution would give(1/(2/3))/0.6=2.5, but this is not the value at any real admissible angle.
problems.answer: No real admissible angle; formal listed value2.5.
problems.note: The source condition sinαcosα=2/3 exceeds the maximum 1/2 and is inconsistent over the reals.

problems.title: Sine rule with an angle ratio
problems.question: Triangle angles are in ratio3:4:5. Its shortest side is 2. Find the middle-length side.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: The angles are 45°,60°,75°. Side lengths are proportional to their sines.
steps: The middle side is 2sin60°/sin45°=√6.

problems.title: Root squares determine a parameter
problems.question: The roots of x²+5x−a=0 have squared sum 33. Find a.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Root sum is −5, product −a. Thus squared sum is 25+2a.
steps: Set25+2a=33 to obtain a=4. The discriminant41>0 confirms two real roots.

problems.title: Even quartic roots occur in pairs
problems.question: x⁴+ax²+b=0 has 4 roots, including−√3 and 2. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Evenness supplies the other roots √3,−2. Thus the polynomial is(x²−3)(x²−4).
steps: Expanding gives a=−7, b=12, sum 5.

problems.title: Fourth powers from Vieta’s formulas
problems.question: If x₁, x₂ solve x²+2x−1=0, find x₁⁴+x₂⁴.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: x₁+x₂=−2, x₁x₂=−1. Hence x₁²+x₂²=4+2=6.
steps: Then x₁⁴+x₂⁴=6²−2(x₁x₂)²=36−2=34.

problems.title: Find a side from an angle bisector
problems.question: AB=12, BC=15, and the bisector from B has length 10. Find AC.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: For adjacent sides b, c and opposite a, the bisector satisfies l²=bc[1−a²/(b+c)²].

problems.title: Three medians and one side
problems.question: One triangle side is 10; the medians to the other sides are 12,9. Find the median to the side 10.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Let a=10. Adding the two median formulas gives 4(m_b²+m_c²)=4a²+b²+c².

problems.title: A rectangle change with fixed original perimeter
problems.question: A rectangle perimeter is 40. Double its width and reduce its length 5; are a increases25. Find the new perimeter.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Let width w, length 20−w. New are a minus old are a is 2w(15−w)−w(20−w)=10w−w².
steps: Setting this equal 25 gives(w−5)²=0. The new dimensions are 10,10, so perimeter40.

problems.title: Binary suffix101
problems.question: How many two-digit decimal integers end in101 when written in binary?
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: The suffix101 means remainder5 modulo8.
steps: The qualifying integers are 13,21,…,93. Their count is(93−13)/8+1=11.

problems.title: Cancel a factored denominator
problems.question: Evaluate[2/(2x+1)−3/(2x²+5x+2)](x²+x−2) at x=√5+1.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: 2x²+5x+2=(2x+1)(x+2). The bracket simplifies to 1/(x+2).
steps: Then multiply by(x+2)(x−1) to get x−1. At the supplied x, the value is √5.

problems.title: Segment between two altitude feet
problems.question: In acute ABC, BB₁, CC₁ are altitudes,∠A=30°, BC=√12. Find B₁C₁.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: The two feet lie on the circle with diameter BC. The angle between their radii gives the standard relation B₁C₁=BC cos A.
steps: Thus B₁C₁=2√3·√3/2=3.

problems.title: Circumradius versus inradius
problems.question: A right triangle has tanα+cotα=25/12. Find circumradius:inradius.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: With legs a, b, hypotenuse c, we have(a²+b²)/(ab)=c²/(ab)=25/12. Scale to a=3, b=4, c=5.
steps: Indeed the resulting leg ratio satisfies t+1/t=25/12, so these are the triangle’s proportions. R=c/2=2.5 and r=(a+b−c)/2=1.

problems.title: Domain reduces a polynomial’s roots
problems.question: Count real roots of(3x⁵−10x³+3x)√(x−1)=0.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: The domain is x≥1. The polynomial factors as x(3x²−1)(x²−3).
steps: Among its roots, only √3 is in the domain. The radical itself adds root 1. Thus there are 2 distinct roots.

problems.title: A substitution for x²+x
problems.question: Find the root sum of 3/(1+x+x²)=3−x²−x.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Put t=x²+x. The denominator t+1 is always positive. Then 3=(3−t)(1+t), so t(t−2)=0.
steps: For t=0, roots are 0,−1; for t=2, roots are 1,−2. Their sum is −2.

problems.title: Factor a two-variable quadratic
problems.question: Count solution pairs of x²+8xy+15y²=0, xy=−6.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: The first equation factors as(x+3y)(x+5y)=0.
steps: If x=−3y, then y²=2, giving2 pairs. If x=−5y, then y²=6/5, giving2 different pairs. Total4.

problems.title: Circumradius of an isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has bases11,21 and legs13. Find its circumradius.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Height=√(13²−5²)=12. Put bases at(±21/2,0),(±11/2,12); centre is(0, k).
steps: Equating distances gives 441/4+k²=121/4+(12−k)², so k=8/3.

problems.title: Integer sides of obtuse triangles
problems.question: For how many integers x do5,7, x for m an obtuse triangle?
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Triangle inequalities require2<x<12. If7 is largest, obtuseness needs49>25+x²; this gives x=3,4.
steps: If x is largest, need x²>25+49=74, giving x=9,10,11. Total5 values.

problems.title: Count tournament participants
problems.question: A tournament has 2 women. Every pair plays2 games. Men-versus-men games exceed men-versus-women games by 66. Find all participants.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: With m men, the counts are m(m−1) and 4m.
steps: Thus m²−5m−66=(m−11)(m+6)=0, so m=11. Including2 women gives 13.

problems.title: A system with exactly one solution
problems.question: Find the sum of p-values for which13x+y=−3, y−px²=−x+1 has exactly 1 solution pair.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Substitution gives px²+12x+4=0.
steps: If p=0, it is linear with 1 root. If p≠0, exactly 1 root requires discriminant144−16p=0, p=9.
The parameter sum is 0+9=9.

problems.title: Exactly two roots of an absolute-value equation
problems.question: Count integer a-values for which x²−2√(a+3)|x|+a−5=0 has exactly 2 real roots.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Require a≥−3 and put t=|x|≥0. The two algebraic t-roots are √(a+3)±2√2.
steps: Exactly one is positive and the other negative when−3≤a<5; this yields2 x-roots. At a=5, there is also x=0, so 3 roots; for a>5, there are 4.
The integer parameters are −3,−2,−1,0,1,2,3,4:eight values.

problems.title: Trisect the108° apex angle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has apex108°, trisected by two cevians. The central base segment is 1. Find the whole base.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: Let base points D, E cut by the cevians. Triangle BDE has apex36°, so BD=1/(2sin18°). Outer triangle ABD has equal angles36° at A, B, so AD=BD.
steps: By symmetry, EC=AD. Hence AC=1+2BD=1+1/sin18°.
Using sin18°=(√5−1)/4 gives AC=2+√5.

problems.title: A diagonal identity determines angles
problems.question: A parallelogram has sides a, b, diagonals d₁, d₂, and a⁴+b⁴=d₁²d₂². Find the difference of adjacent angles.
problems.idea: Use root identities, quadratic substitutions, and standard geometric formulas; check feasibility first.
formulas: For included angleθ, d₁²d₂²=(a²+b²)²−4a²b²cos²θ.
steps: The given identity leaves2a²b²(1−2cos²θ)=0. Since a, b>0, cos²θ=1/2, so adjacent angles are 45°,135°.
Their difference is 90°.
